name: project risks
description: An invented project in which the person takes part, asked the same standing question after each event: confirmed risks, a concern not yet measured, an unrelated update, a risk resolved, a concern that becomes a risk, and a corrected date. Repeated dreams with nothing new.

records.author: @you
records.text: Harrow risk review, February 1: two confirmed risks. First, the payment vendor contract ends on March 31 and no renewal is signed, so checkout stops on April 1 if nothing is done. Second, only one engineer knows the billing code, and she leaves in April.
records.title: Harrow risk review

records.author: data engineer
records.text: I have a vague worry the daily usage import is getting slower. No numbers yet, just a feeling.

records.author: @you
records.text: Let's treat that as a concern to watch, not a risk, until someone measures it.

records.author: data engineer
records.text: Fair, I'll measure it when I can.

questions.question: What are the Harrow project's current risks, and what supports each?
questions.expectedAnswer: Two confirmed risks: the payment vendor contract ends March 31 with no renewal signed (checkout would stop April 1), and only one engineer knows the billing code and she leaves in April. A slower usage import is an unmeasured concern, not a risk.

records.author: @you
records.text: Harrow's office moves to the fourth floor on February 20. Nothing changes for the project's work.
records.title: Harrow office move

questions.question: What are the Harrow project's current risks, and what supports each?
questions.expectedAnswer: Unchanged: the unsigned payment vendor renewal before March 31, and the single engineer who knows the billing code leaving in April. The slower import is still an unmeasured concern.

records.author: finance lead
records.text: The payment vendor renewal is signed, through March 2035.

records.author: @you
records.text: Great, so the checkout risk is closed.

questions.question: What are the Harrow project's current risks, and what supports each?
questions.expectedAnswer: One confirmed risk: only one engineer knows the billing code and she leaves in April. The vendor contract risk is closed: the renewal was signed on February 24 through March 2035. The slower import remains an unmeasured concern.

records.author: data engineer
records.text: Measured the usage import: it went from 20 minutes to 95 minutes over February, and at this rate it overruns the morning reports by mid-March.

records.author: @you
records.text: Then the import is a real risk now, not just a worry.

records.author: engineering manager
records.text: Correction on the billing risk: the billing engineer is staying until July, not leaving in April. We still need a second person on billing.

records.author: @you
records.text: Noted, July then. Still a risk.

questions.question: What are the Harrow project's current risks, and what supports each?
questions.expectedAnswer: Two confirmed risks: the usage import grew from 20 to 95 minutes over February and will overrun the morning reports by mid-March; and only one engineer knows the billing code, now leaving in July (corrected from April). The vendor contract risk is closed (renewed through March 2035).

questions.question: What are the Harrow project's current risks, and what supports each?
questions.expectedAnswer: The usage import overrunning the morning reports by mid-March, and the single billing engineer leaving in July. The vendor risk is closed.
